svg.aria-label: pqtls-lab handshake flow showing where downgrade rejection happens.
svg.title: pqtls-lab handshake and policy enforcement
svg.desc: A TLS 1.3 handshake between pqtls-client and pqtls-server, showing the two post-handshake checks: certificate and hostname verification, then verification of the negotiated group against the profile. A violation terminates the connection before any application data is sent.
svg.text: Handshake flow and downgrade rejection
Profile: hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 — groups: [X25519MLKEM768], fallback.allow_classical: false
pqtls-client
pqtls-server
Both sides configure ONLY the profile's groups.
An unknown group name aborts — never a silent default.
TCP connect
ClientHello
SNI · ALPN pqtls1 · key_share for X25519MLKEM768 only
ServerHello, Certificate, CertificateVerify, Finished
selected group · ECDSA P-256 signature
CHECK 1
Verify the certificate chain and hostname
chain · validity dates · subjectAltName via SSL_set1_host
first, because an unverified peer's claims mean nothing
CHECK 2
Verify the NEGOTIATED group vs. the profile
read back with SSL_get0_group_name (case-insensitive)
the server runs the identical check, independently
Both peers check. Relying on the client alone would leave
a server quietly serving classical connections under a
hybrid profile.
✗ Negotiated group violates the profile
Terminate immediately. No application data is ever sent.
Record error_category: "tls-policy" — distinct from "handshake",
so a policy rejection is never mistaken for a broken network.
✓ Compliant — exchange application data
uint32 length prefix + validated UTF-8 JSON
one SSL_read is not one message: frames are reassembled
close_notify · one JSONL metrics record per peer
What this connection does and does not provide
✓ Post-quantum KEY ESTABLISHMENT — session keys resist a future quantum adversary, so recorded traffic stays confidential.
✗ Post-quantum AUTHENTICATION — the server signed with classical ECDSA. A quantum adversary able to forge signatures
DURING a live handshake could still impersonate it. The connection is therefore NOT end-to-end quantum-safe.
